(By Pleader Shri Gopal) *J U D G M E N T

* This judgment is emerged consequent upon the petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of M.V. Act, claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/, on account of the injuries sustained by her, in a road traffic accident.

*FACTS OF THE CASE IN NUTSHELL*
Smt.M.C.Rajeshwari vs Icici Lombard General on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175451597/
1 2.

Facts leading to the case of the petitioner forthcoming in the petition that, on 9.6.2021, at about 7.20 a.m. to 7.30 a.m., the petitioner being the pedestrian, walking from K.P. Agrahara towards Cholurpalya, 2nd cross, near Ganesh Medical, at the same time, the Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA02AD7570, driven by its driver, in a rash and negligent manner,
consequently, hit the petitioner.
As a result, the petitioner fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

3. It is further stated in the petition that, immediately, the petitioner was shifted Shanthi Clinic,
Magadi road, Bengaluru wherein, first aid treatment was taken, then she was shifted to Sanjaygandhi Trauma & Orthopaedic Centre, Byrasandra, Bengaluru, wherein, she was admitted as an inpatient.

It is stated that, the petitioner had incurred Rs.1,00,000/ towards hospitalization,
conveyance, medical treatment and other incidental charges etc.
4.
It is also stated in the petition that, prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 66 years, doing coolie and used to earn a sum of Rs.700/ per day.
Due to the accidental injuries, she has suffered mental shock and agony and she could not work as she was earlier to the accident.
5. It is alleged in the petition that, the accident was occurred due to the rash and negligent act of the driver of the Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA02AD7570.
In this regard, case was registered against the driver by the jurisdictional Magadi Traffic police as per Crime No.14/2021 for the offences punishable under Sec. 279 and 337 of IPC.
As such, the respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
6. After service of the notice of this petition, the respondents have appeared through their respective counsel, and filed the written statements, in answer to the case of the petitioner.
7. The respondent No.1, in the written statement has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
It is the contention of this respondent that, Goods Autorickshaw bearing No.KA01AD7570, was not at all involved in the alleged accident.
Further contended that, complaint has been lodged before the jurisdictional police with all malafide intention, after a lapse of 3 days.
Further, admitted about the issuance of the policy in respect of autorickshaw bearing registration N.KA02AD7570 and its validity, as on the date of the accident.
It is the contention of the respondent that, the accident was occurred due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner.
It is specifically contended that, the driver of the offending vehicle was not possessed valid and effective driving license and thereby violated the terms and conditions of the policy.
Further contended that, auto rickshaw was used without having valid permit and fitness certificate.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition, against the company.
8. The respondent No.2 in its written statement has not seriously disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the petitioner.
But, strongly denied the allegation of the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
It is contention of the respondent No.2 that, the compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive and exorbitant.
With all these main grounds, prayed to dismiss the petition.

Smt.M.C.Rajeshwari vs Icici Lombard General on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175451597/
2 9.

On the basis of the rival pleadings of both the parties, for final determination of this case,
following issues were framed:
*ISSUES*
1. Whether the petitioner proves that she had sustained grievous injuries in an accident that was taken place on 9.6.2021 at about 7.20 to 7.30 a.m. near Cholarapalya 2nd cross, near Ganesha Medicals, Cholarapalya, Bengaluru due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA 02AD7570 in an actionable negligence?
2.
Whether the petitioner is entitled for compensation as prayed for?
If so, at what rate?

From whom?
3. What order or award?
10.

In order to substantiate the case of the petitioner, by name Smt.M.C.Rajeshwari during the course of evidence, placed her affidavit evidence, in lieu of examinationinchief, who examined as PW1 in the case on hand.
At the time of her evidence, 12 documentary evidence got marked as Ex.P1 to Ex.P12.
In addition to her evidence, placed the evidence of the Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. as PW2.
At the time of his evidence placed two documents marked as Ex.P13 & Ex.P14, for consideration.
11. On the other hand, to prove the defenses forthcoming in the objection, the respondents have not adduced any rebuttal evidence for consideration.

After completion of the evidence of both the side,
matter was set down for arguments.
12. Heard the argument of both the counsel.
Perused the materials available on record.

13. On appreciation of the evidence available on record, my findings to the aforesaid issues are as follows:
 Issue No.1: In the Affirmative.

Issue No.2: Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.3: As per final order  For the following:
 *R E A S O N S*
 ISSUE NO.1:
14.

It is the case of the petitioner Smt.M.C. Rajeshwari that, due to the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA02AD 7570,
alleged accident had taken place.
Consequently, the petitioner had sustained grievous injuries.

On the other hand, the respondents though not disputed the accident and the injuries sustained by the Smt.M.C.Rajeshwari vs Icici Lombard General on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175451597/
3 petitioner, strongly denied the allegation of actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.

sentences.text: But not adduced any evidence in this regard for consideration.

In such a situation,
duty is more on the part of the court, to assess the evidence available on record in order to come to the proper conclusion.
15. Onus probandi is on the petitioner, to prove the above issue, on the touch stone of preponderance of probabilities.
To discharge the burden lies on the petitionerM.C.Rajeshwari placed her affidavit evidence by reiterating the main petition averments.

To demonstrate the stand of the petitioner, about the accident, produced police papers as per Ex.P1 toEx.P8 and medical documents as per Ex.P9 to Ex.P11 along with her Aadhar card and also the evidence of PW2 along with documents Ex.P13 & Ex.P14, with respect to the proof of disabilities sustained by her consequent upon the accident.
16. Among the documentary evidence, in proof of above issue, Ex.P1 to Ex.P8 are the material documents.
On taking birds eye view towards the said documents, go to show that, alleged accident was occurred on 9.6.2021 and first information in this regard was given by the petitioner on 12.6.2021.

In connection with 4 days delay in giving first information is concerned, it is noted in the recitals of the complaint, as well as in column No.3(c) of the Ex.P1 that, after the accident since she was taking treatment in the hospital and due to pain while taking rest in the home, she approached the doctor in belated stage, and belated complaint was filed.

With respect to the reasons noted in the said documents on the point of delay, have not been seriously questioned by the other side, by placing contra materials, to suspect about the reasons noted in the said document.
Hence, the point of delay in giving first information is not fatal in the case on hand.

17. Apart from this, it is to be noted that, by virtue of information given by the petitioner, criminal law set in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle, on the allegation that he has committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 337 of IPC and in the recitals of the Ex.P1 & Ex.P2,
there is a clear narration about the actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle on the fateful day of the accident.
Added to this the spot mahazar said to have executed, after setting criminal law in motion against the driver of the offending vehicle.

and the police notice as well as reply notice marked at Ex.P3 to Ex.P5 respectively, and IMV report marked at Ex.P6, wound certificate Ex.P7 depict about the involvement of the offending vehicle in the said accident, and also name of the driver of the offending vehicle at the time of accident.
It is the opinion of the IMV inspector that, the said accident was not due to any mechanical defect of the vehicle involved in the accident.
Further, in the wound certificate it is evident that, on the history of RTA, the petitioner had sustained injuries.

And the sketch annexed to the mahazar remained unquestioned by the other side to prove the innocence of the driver of the offending vehicle and to prove the defense of the other side that, due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner while crossing the road, accident in question had taken place.
All these material and convincing documents in proof of the case of the petitioner against the driver of the offending vehicle remained unshaken by the other side.
18. Ultimately, on going through the charge sheet submitted by the investigation officer as per Ex.P8, and the allegation forthcoming in the column No.17 of the said document, go to show that,

due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle, by name Ramu accident and Smt.M.C.Rajeshwari vs Icici Lombard General on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175451597/
4 its consequences were taken place.
Accordingly, final report was submitted against him, on the allegation that, he had committed the offences punishable under section 279 and 338 of IPC.

Though the said document is not substantive piece of evidence, in the absence of contra materials,
the said document can be treated as conclusive proof in support of the case of the petitioner.

19. At the time of crossexamination of PW1, though several questions put to this witness, no effort has been made out to elicit the material point that, due to the negligence on the part of the petitioner, accident in question had taken place and also to prove the innocence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
At the same time, no rebuttal evidence from the side of the respondents to impeach the evidence given by the petitioner, in support of the above issue.
Hence, the petitioner has placed reliable evidence for consideration to prove the above issue.

20. In the light of the evidence placed on record, by the petitioner, in the case on hand, by way of affidavit and the documentary evidence, speak that, the alleged accident was occurred, due to the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle.
On the other hand, the respondents have utterly failed to prove all the defenses forthcoming in the written statements, by placing acceptable evidence on record.

Accordingly, I am of the view that, the petitioner has placed satisfactory evidence to prove the above issue to the effect that, the alleged accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Autorickshaw bearing registration No.KA 02AD7570.
Hence, without making much discussion on the point of the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, I am answering the Issue No.1, in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.2 :
21.
This issue is with respect to the entitlement of reliefs claimed by the petitioner.
The petitioner through this petition claiming compensation of Rs.10,00,000/ on account of the injuries sustained by him in the accident, under different heads.

22. Before appreciation of the evidence placed by the petitioner about the injuries sustained by him,
in the accident and its consequences, it is apt to note herein, the preposition laid down in the following land mark judgment, while appreciating the injury cases in Motor Vehicle Act.
Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another.

entities.text: Civil Appeal No.8981/2010 D.D. 18.10.2010 Rajkumar V/s Ajay Kumar & Another
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: "In the aforesaid case, it was held that, the court has to make judicious attempt to award compensation to the loss suffered by the claimant.
The compensation should not be assessed conservatively.
On the other hand, compensation should also not be endeavouring to secure some uniformity and consistency.

The object of awarding compensation is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done, as far as money can do so, in a fair reasonable and equitable manner."
23.

In the light of the preposition laid down in the above case, it is also relevant to note that, "while determining quantum of compensation, in such cases, the court has to strike a balance between the inflated and unreasonable demands of a victim and the equally untenable claim of the opposite Smt.M.C.Rajeshwari vs Icici Lombard General on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175451597/
5
party saying
that nothing is payable
. That sympathy for the victim does not, and should not, comes in the way of making a correct assessment.
But if a case is made out, and the court must not be chary of awarding adequate compensation.

"
24. In connection with the injuries sustained by the petitioner, had produced wound certificate marked at Ex.P7.
The said document discloses that, he sustained the following injuries: Fracture femur right 25.
According to the doctor, the aforesaid injury is grievous in nature.
Apart from this, the petitioner has produced, discharge summary, medical bills & prescriptions marked as per Ex.P9 to Ex.P11.
In addition to his evidence, got examined Dr.Chidanand K.J.C. as PW2 and placed entire case sheet and xray as per Ex.P13 & Ex.P14, for consideration.

As per the discharge summary marked at Ex.P9, the petitioner had taken treatment as an inpatient at Sanjaygandhi Institute of Trauma &
Orthopaedics from 11.6.2021 to 21.6.2021.

For having taken the note of the nature of the injuries sustained by her, and by keeping in mind about her sufferings during the said period of treatment,
in connection with the grievous injuries, and by considering the mode of treatment given to the petitioner, in the hospital, I am of the view that, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.40,000/ towards pain and suffering.
26.
Another point to be discussed herein, about the loss of income during laid up period and rest period.
In the petition, she has stated that, she was working as a coolie and getting an income of Rs.700/ per day.
To substantiate this, she has not placed any iota of documents to show the income of Rs.700/ per day.
On the other hand, it is to be noted that, the injuries sustained by her are grievous in nature, as per the wound certificate.
On going through the discharge summaries marked at Ex.P9, the petitioner had taken treatment as an inpatient at Sanjaygandhi Institute of Trauma & Orthopaedics from 11.6.2021 to 21.6.2021.
Hence, definitely, there was some difficulty to her, during the period of treatment, to do daily routine work and to do her work for livelihood at least for one month.
At the time of fracture, it is very difficult for her, to do her work, as she was earlier during the period of treatment.
Hence, I am of the view that, she is entitled for compensation of Rs.15,000/ towards loss of income during the laid up period and rest period.

27. The petitioner herein, in connection with her treatment expenses, at the time of her evidence,
placed 13 medical bills of Rs.17,264/ as per Ex.P10 along with prescriptions as per Ex.P11.
Other side not seriously denied the said document except suggesting that, the petitioner has placed created medical bills for consideration.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.17,264/
under the head of medical expenses.
28. The petitioner herein, as per the medical records, had sustained grievous injuries of "right IT fracture (boyd and griffin type II."
As per the evidence of the petitioner, she took treatment in Sanjaygandhi hospital and later discharged with the advice of followup treatment.
As such, during the period of treatment, she could have spent some amount towards travelling, food and nourishment and for attendant.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.10,000/
towards attendant charges, food, and nourishment and conveyance charges.

Smt.M.C.Rajeshwari vs Icici Lombard General on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175451597/
6 29.
Another material point of loss of future income is concerned, the petitioner herein, asserting that, she has sustained permanent disability, consequent upon the injuries sustained by her.

In order to prove the same, the petitioner has relied on her evidence along with the wound certificate,
along with other medical documents.
In the evidence of the PW1, reiterated the same thing forthcoming in the main petition.
As already discussed above, wound certificate placed by him as per Ex.P7, goes to show that, she had sustained "Right IT fracture (boyd and griffin type II)".
To substantiate this, the petitioner has placed, wound certificate, Xray and other medical documents for consideration.
Added to this, placed the evidence of Dr. Chidanand K.J.C., as PW2, to prove the disability sustained by the petitioner, consequent upon the accident.
30. In the evidence of PW2, deposed that, on the history of RTA, the petitioner had been to Sanjaygandhi Hospital.
On diagnosis found, Right IT fracture'.
In this regard, he underwent treatment in the form of CRIF with PFN on 15.6.2021 and discharged on 21.6.2021.

At the time of his examination to assess the disability on 15.4.2022 noted the points that, there is a restriction in the range of movements of right knee hip, healed scar mark over right hip quadriceps wasting,
associated with pain on movements on knee hip, and difficulty to do daily activities like cross leg sitting, squatting and using the Indian toilet and also difficulty in right limb.

Further deposed that,
Xray shown malunited fracture with implants in situ.

After assessment of mobility and stability components and by giving additional points as per Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment of Government of India and also on the basis of assessment of permanent physical disability of lower limb, range movements of hip knee ankle and foot, came to the conclusion that the petitioner has got permanent physical disability with respect to particular limb 51% and whole body disability is 17%.

entities.text: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Further opined that, the petitioner has to undergo survey for implants removal which requires approximately Rs.25,000/ and also may require total hip replacement in future.
In support of the evidence of this witness, placed Ex.P13 & Ex.P14 for consideration.

31. At the time of crossexamination PW2 admitted that, he was the treated doctor and the petitioner received little bit medical expenses through Ayushman Bharath Yojana, and there was injury to the petitioner near hip joint and he has not given any disability certificate to the petitioner,
and in connection with the question put this witness about further treatment of the petitioner, he simply answered that, in connection with his further treatment, noted in the outpatient record and denied the suggestion that, there was no any disability and problems to the petitioner, but admitted that, there was no any injury caused to the knee ankle and foot of the petitioner, and denied the suggestion of the other side that, he assessed the disability of the petitioner with respect to whole body in higher side and also expressed his opinion about the approximate future medical expenses in higher side.
But stated that, the petitioner sustained type II fracture, as such, the fractured bones are malunited.

Over all appreciation of evidence of PW2, along with medical documents, nature of the injuries sustained by the petitioner and mode of treatment taken by the petitioner, I am of the view that, the percentage of disability expressed by the PW2 with respect to the whole body, seems little bit exorbitant.
As such, by looking into the nature of the fracture sustained by the petitioner, I am of the view that, whole body disability is apt to be taken as 14% instead of 17%.
The same will meet the ends of justice.

Smt.M.C.Rajeshwari vs Icici Lombard General on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175451597/
7 32.
In connection with the age of the petitioner is concerned, on going through the cause title of the petition reveals that, as on the date of the petition, her age was 66 years.

In support of the age proof,
she has placed Aadhar as per Ex.P12 for consideration.
On going through the Aadhar card her date of birth was mentioned as 31.7.1960.
The accident occurred on 9.6.2021.
Therefore, as on the date of accident the age of the petitioner was 61 years.
Hence, it is apt to consider the age of the petitioner as 61 years.
To the said age as per Sarla Verma case, multiplier '7' is to be taken into consideration.

33. Next factual aspect of the income of the petitioner is concerned, in the main petition, and also in the examinationinchief evidence, it is the assertion of the petitioner that, prior to the accident,
she was doing coolie and earning Rs.700/ per day.
But there is no iota of documents to show the definite income of the petitioner per day prior to the date of accident.
In such a situation, as per law notional income has to be taken in to consideration.
But the said notional income is to be taken judiciously, by taking into consideration of the year of the accident.
As per the notional income chart, I am of the view that, it is apt to take the notional income of the petitioner as Rs.15,000/ for the year 2021.

34. In the light of my detailed discussions held above, no doubt injuries sustained by the petitioner definitely come in the way of her future, to do her daily routine work, as well as to do his work for livelihood.
Since, the hand and fingers are vital organs, to do day to day activities.

Hence, the petitioner herein, is entitled for compensation under loss of future income as follows:
Rs.15,000 X 12 X 7 X14/100= Rs.1,76,400/
35.
Next factual aspect loss of amenities is concerned, due to the accidental injuries, definitely, the petitioner will suffer in future, both physically and functionally.

All the medical records and the evidence of PW2, substantiates that, the due to the disability of the petitioner she will suffer a lot in future also, while doing her day today activities as well as to do her avocation for her livelihood, as well as to maintain her family members.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for Rs.25,000/ towards loss of amenities.

36. In connection with the future medication expenses is concerned, the PW2 at the time of his evidence, has stated that the petitioner requires one more surgery for removal of implants and also required total hip replacement approximate cost has been mentioned as Rs.25,000/.
But in connection with the hip replacement no expenses mentioned in the affidavit evidence of PW2.
At the same time, with respect to the removal of implants expenses no estimation is available on record.
Hence, the petitioner is entitled for any compensation of Rs.20,000/ under the head of future medication.

37. In view of my due discussions held above, on various aspects, the petitioner is entitled for compensation in to to, under the following heads:
 Compensation heads Compensation  amount  1.
Pain and
Suffering Rs. 40,00000
Smt.M.C.Rajeshwari vs Icici Lombard General on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175451597/
8 2. Loss of income during Rs. 15,00000 laidup period and rest period
3. Medical expenses Rs. 17,26400 4.Attendant, Rs. 10,00000 Nourishment and Conveyance Charges 5. Loss of future income Rs.1,76,40000 6. Loss of Amenities Rs. 25,00000
7.Future medication Rs. 20,00000 Total Rs.3,03,66400 38.

Accordingly, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,03,664/ (Rupees three lakhs three thousand six hundred and sixty four only) along with interest @ 6% per annum, as per the proposition laid down by the Honourable High court of Karnataka in MFA No.103557/2016,
Between Sri Ram General Insurance Company Limited V/S. Lakshmi And Others dated.
20.03.2018.

. 
LIABILITY:
39.

In so far as, liability is concerned, it is the assertion of the petitioners that, the respondent No.1 being the insurance company of the offending vehicle and the respondent No.2 being the owner are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the petitioners,
On the other hand, the respondent No.1, in the case on hand, has not seriously disputed the existence of the insurance policy, as on the date of the accident.
And no evidence is available on record, to show that, there is a violation of the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, by its owner.
40. As per the records, the policy was in force from 15.10.2020 to 14.10.2021.
Alleged accident had taken place on 9.6.2021.
As such, the respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners, as per the order of this court.
However, the respondent No.1, being the insurance company has to indemnify the loss of the respondent No.2, towards the payment of award amount.

Resultantly,
I am answering the issue No.2 partly in the Affirmative.

ISSUE NO.3:
41.

In view of my due discussions on issue Nos.1 & 2, I proceed to pass the following;
*O R D E R* The claim petition filed by the petitioner U/S 166 of MV Act is hereby partly allowed with costs.

Smt.M.C.Rajeshwari vs Icici Lombard General on 15 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/175451597/
9

The petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.3,03,664/ (Rupees three lakhs three thousand six hundred and sixty four only), along with the interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of the petition till the date of deposit.
The respondents are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

In view of the valid insurance policy the respondent No.1 insurance company is liable to pay the compensation determined by this court, with interest at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till its realization within two months from the date of this order.
The expenses to be incurred for future medication shall not carry any interest.
After deposit of the compensation amount with interest, 40% is directed to be deposited in any Nationalized/Scheduled bank in F.D for a period of 3 years.
And remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner through due process of law.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.500/.
Draw award accordingly.
